d: On 21 April 1526, Babur lined up about 700 bullock carts on the open plain of Panipat, tied them together with leather ropes and placed his cannons behind them. Ibrahim Lodi's elephants panicked at the guns, and by the end of the day the Mughal empire had begun. Panipat would see two more battles that decided who ruled Delhi. Five hundred years later, something is arriving from abroad again. This time it comes in shipping containers: used clothes thrown away in the US, the UK, Germany and Japan, shipped to Kandla port in Gujarat and trucked to Panipat, now called the cast-off capital of…
